evidence.title: The trust collapse: Infinite AI content is awful - Arnon Shimoni
evidence.text: The trust collapse: Infinite AI content is awful - Arnon Shimoni Skip to content Arnon Shimoni About Arnon Shimoni Now The trust collapse: Infinite AI content is awful We’re living through the weirdest moment in human history. For the first time since, well, ever, the cost of creating content has dropped to essentially zero. Not “cheaper than before”, but like actually free. It’s so easy to generate a thousand blog posts or ten thousand “””personalized””” emails and it barely costs you anything (for now). In theory this sounds great, infinite content. Giving words to those who struggled before. So many opportunities. But if you’re trying to sell, trust is collapsing faster than content is proliferating. And I don’t mean “trust” in some abstract sense, but the real – who’s real, who’s credible, and what should I be paying attention to? We’re not moving forward. We’re definitely moving backwards. A tale of a B2B SaaS company I know someone who runs a B2B SaaS company’s sales – he’s very smart. He spent many many years building his network and being a “relationship builder” type of seller – earning trust the old-fashioned way. When we spoke last Sunday, he told me “I ignore all email outreach, and I barely even pick up the phone if I don’t know who it is” “I can’t tell if it’s a real person or someone who’s scraped my details. I used to be able to tell. Now I can’t. So I just… don’t engage. Not worth my time.” To dumb it down for you if you’re doing this outbound – he’s not asking “do I need this product?” that you’re selling, but he’s asking “why should I trust you specifically to deliver it?” – and you’re not getting through with that. evidence.snippet:
Hello, Hacker News community! I’m Gary, the founder of Vizard.ai. I am thrilled to introduce you to our cutting-edge AI video editing tool that is designed to help content creators/marketers/businesses alike to repurpose long-form webinar/event/speech videos into bite-size social-ready highlights.

As a beginner in video editing, I struggled with the complexity of professional video editing software like Adobe Premiere Pro or Apple Final Cut Pro. I found it overwhelming and challenging to use, and I would eventually abandon my efforts to edit videos. But I knew that video content creation was important, and I was determined to find a solution.

Being an expert in AI, I decided to use my knowledge to simplify video editing. That's when I came up with the idea for Vizard.ai.

I have trained several deep learning models that work together to simplify the video editing process. The first model is a computer vision model that segments the video into pieces. The second model is a speech-to-text model that transcribes the voice in the video. The last model is a scene change detector model that detects changes in the video.

When I combined these three models, I was able to edit the video like editing a picture. I could trim the video by transcript text, making the process much simpler and more intuitive.

Our tool is intuitive, easy to use, and designed to simplify the video editing process for beginners. With Vizard.ai, content creators, marketers, and businesses can quickly and efficiently repurpose long-form video content into bite-size social-ready highlights, increasing their reach and engagement on social media.

I am excited to share my story and the story of Vizard.ai with the Hacker News community. Thank you for your time and consideration, and I look forward to your feedback and questions.
